findings.clause: C1: Every table has TENANT_ID BIGINT NOT NULL, FK_<TABLE>_TENANT → CORE_TENANT(ID), an index led by TENANT_ID, every UNIQUE composite with TENANT_ID
findings.problem: ADR-CAT-054 removed the 12 FK_<TABLE>_TENANT constraints to satisfy factory contract C6.15. The erp-core checklist requires those constraints and treats any 'no' as a rejection, so the library rule wins.
findings.fix: Restore FK_<TABLE>_TENANT → CORE_TENANT(ID) on all 12 tables. Supersede ADR-CAT-054 with an ADR that records the given tenant table as a permitted given reference. File a platform finding against C6.15 so the rule exempts the given tenancy FK. Update D-P2-03 and registry-db.

findings.clause: F4: Direct file-system or S3 access for business content, or a multipart endpoint of the module (and C7: every byte goes through the FILE endpoints)
findings.problem: API-CAT-018 (image upload) and API-CAT-049 (xlsx import) are multipart endpoints of CAT, with their own CAT-413 and CAT-415 rows. The checklist forbids any multipart endpoint in a module.
findings.fix: The client uploads through the given FILE endpoints: the public image store for images, the private store for the import file. The CAT endpoints then take a fileDocumentRef in JSON and read the bytes through FileDocumentLookupApi. Update the api-spec, the Error Catalog (drop the 413 and 415 rows), F1–F4 of SCR-CAT-001 and SCR-CAT-004, and the TCs. If the core lacks a capability for this, write CORE-GAP-<topic> instead.

findings.clause: F7: A second export path: a CSV / XLSX / PDF writer, an /export endpoint, a report permission of your own
findings.problem: API-CAT-048 builds an xlsx workbook in memory and serves it through its own endpoint. That is a CAT-owned XLSX writer, which F7 forbids.
findings.fix: Provide the import sheet as a ReportProvider bean (CatItemImportSheetReportProvider) served through the given report engine and PrintApi / PrintResponses, the same way the label PDF is already served.

findings.clause: C3 / F2: Every native query names TENANT_ID and its method carries @TenantUnscoped(reason, adr)
findings.problem: The QR catalog says the tenant filter is 'implied'. QR-CAT-006, 008, 009 and 037 are native queries, and the recursive steps of QR-CAT-006 and 037 read CAT_CATEGORY without TENANT_ID. ADR-CAT-047 makes no @TenantUnscoped decision.
findings.fix: Write TENANT_ID = :tenant into every native QR, including each recursive step and each EXISTS sub-select. Record in ADR-CAT-047 that these methods carry @TenantUnscoped(reason, adr = ADR-CAT-047).

findings.clause: P2 closure: what happens when a record is absent (seeds in tenants other than PLATFORM)
findings.problem: Narrowed from round 1. The lookup and number-series seeds at TENANT_ID = 1 follow checklist lines C5 and C9, so they are correct. The 8 rows of CAT_UNIT_EINVOICE_CODE are different: CAT owns that table, every read is tenant-filtered, and the rows exist only for tenant 1. In every real tenant, Variant and Item-unit reads therefore return an empty einvoiceUnitCode. ADR-CAT-046 §3 leaves the copy mechanism unowned, and precondition S0 assumes the 8 rows exist in every test tenant.
findings.fix: Name the given tenant-provisioning hook in an SRS A9 given-usage row. Add a CAT contributor to the bootstrap block that copies the 8 Unit e-invoice codes into each new tenant, and add a TC for it. If the given has no such hook, write CORE-GAP-tenant-seed-provisioning and record an OPEN platform finding owned by erp-core.

findings.clause: P1 silent path: deactivating an Item or a Variant leaves its barcodes active
findings.problem: API-CAT-004 does not deactivate the Item's Variants or barcodes. QR-CAT-052 checks only that the Variant is active, not the Item, so a deactivated Item still resolves at the point of sale. UQ_CAT_BARCODE_VALUE keeps the GTIN locked to the dead record, and RULE-CAT-029 then names a deactivated Item. No statement or TC covers this.
findings.fix: Add an unwanted-pattern REQ and a RULE: a barcode lookup returns no Variant of an inactive Item. Choose one of two fixes: deactivate the barcodes together with their Variant, or exclude barcodes of inactive Variants from uniqueness and from QR-CAT-048. Add a join on CAT_ITEM.IS_ACTIVE_FL to QR-CAT-052, and add TCs.

findings.clause: P4 pattern: invariants checked only at create can be broken by later transitions
findings.problem: (a) API-CAT-005 checks only the name when it reactivates an Item. RULE-CAT-025 ignores inactive Items, and RULE-CAT-015 protects only active Items, so a reactivated Item can sit in an inactive Category or have no active Variant. (b) RULE-CAT-031 applies on create only, so deactivating an Item unit (API-CAT-013) leaves active barcodes bound to that unit.
findings.fix: On reactivation, re-check RULE-CAT-026 and require at least one active Variant, either by refusing or by reactivating the default Variant. Add a RULE that refuses deactivating an Item unit while an active barcode uses it, with a {count} placeholder. Add a catalog row and a TC for each.

findings.clause: P3 read-binding: does every foreign id a screen renders resolve to a label
findings.problem: CATEGORY-OPTIONS-QUERY reads only active Categories, yet it also labels the categoryFk shown in the list and the header. An Item in a Category that was deactivated later renders an unresolved id.
findings.fix: Label categoryFk from an unfiltered tree read under a separate cache key, and keep the active-only read for the select options. Add a frontend TC.

findings.clause: P1 / engine concurrency check: a guard has a statement but no test case
findings.problem: ADR-CAT-047 and the API blocks name guards against parallel requests: the Item row lock, FOR SHARE reads on components, the Category tree advisory lock and the scale-prefix lock. No TC exercises any of them.
findings.fix: Add two-request backend TCs for: the last two Variants deactivated at once, two generations over the 300 limit, two make-primary calls, a barcode add racing a clashing layout create, two Category moves (A under B and B under A), and a Bundle save racing a component deactivation. Each asserts that exactly one request wins and the other returns its catalog code.

findings.clause: CM-4 / SEC-BE enforcement and the optimistic lock are untested
findings.problem: The PLATFORM-STD rows are excluded from the TCs. No TC shows 403 for a Seller/cashier on a mutation, 401 without a token, CAT-409-STALE-VERSION, or a cross-tenant read returning 404.
findings.fix: Add TCs in package SEC-BE for: a stale version on API-CAT-003; 403 for a Seller/cashier and for a Warehouse user on one CREATE, one UPDATE and one DELETE, following the SRS B4 matrix; 401 without a token; and cross-tenant reads of an Item, a Variant and a Category returning 404.

findings.clause: C18 / C20: the module manifest META-INF/erp/modules/<code>.yaml and the ModuleBoundaryRules test
findings.problem: PHASE CORE declares no module manifest, no api-paths, no ModuleBoundaryRules test and no CI job of the module.
findings.fix: Add a 'Module manifest' block to PHASE CORE: cat.yaml with code CAT, the package (see G16), the six permission modules, api-paths /api/v1/cat/** and an empty dependency list. Add the ModuleBoundaryRules test and a CI job for the module.

findings.problem: The SRS has placeholder headings 'AC-CAT-017 — reserved' and 'AC-CAT-053 — reserved', so each of these ids is defined twice.
findings.fix: Delete both placeholder headings and the note that explains them.

findings.problem: The page and size parameters of API-CAT-038, 040, 042 and 046 have no bounds and no default.
findings.fix: State page ≥ 0 and size 1–100 with default 20, return CAT-400-REQUEST-INVALID outside that range, and add one TC.

findings.problem: Eight codes are routed without a 'text:' binding (ADR-CAT-053 §1).
findings.fix: Add 'text: RULE-CAT-0nn message' to the eight F2 rows, then restore the wording assertions in TC-CAT-130, 143, 144, 145, 150, 157, 165 and 171.

findings.problem: Host data lines exist in about 10 TCs, but the check examined none of them.
findings.fix: Rewrite the Host data lines in the engine form (value, state, creating call), then re-run analyze and confirm a non-zero count.

findings.clause: F8: A copy of a core class, a com.erp.* package in the application, an edit to a core migration
findings.problem: PHASE CORE puts the module under package root com.erp.cat and publishes com.erp.cat.crossmodule.CatalogueReadApi. That is a com.erp.* package in the application. The contract and the test plans repeat the name.
findings.fix: Choose an application root package outside com.erp (for example <org>.commerce.cat) and record it in an ADR. Use it in PHASE CORE, the manifest (G11), CatalogueReadApi and the TCs that name it.

findings.clause: C16: Entities whose changes a reviewer must see carry @Audited(entityType = "<TABLE>", ignore = {…})
findings.problem: The module registry lists erp-core audit as a dependency for 'catalogue change history', and PRD P-5 delegates change history to the given audit. Yet the plan marks no entity @Audited, and SRS A9 has no audit given-usage row.
findings.fix: Declare @Audited on the SHARED master entities (CAT_ITEM, CAT_VARIANT, CAT_CATEGORY, CAT_ITEM_UNIT, CAT_BARCODE, CAT_BUNDLE_COMP) in PHASE CORE / DATA-DOM, and add the audit row to SRS A9 given-usage. Alternatively, remove audit from the registry dependencies with an ADR.

findings.problem: The plan says 'every endpoint checks its permission' but does not place the check in @PreAuthorize on service methods, which C13 requires. API-CAT-047 needs a programmatic check that is not stated. The event topic is given as 'CatalogueChanged', not in the '<code>.<Name>' form that C19 requires.
findings.fix: State that every service method carries @PreAuthorize(CatPermissions.PERM_…), with API-CAT-047 checking programmatically (ADR-CAT-045). Name the topic 'cat.CatalogueChanged' in PHASE CORE and in CON-CAT-018.

findings.problem: ADR-CAT-015, 028 and 031 trace POL-CAT-010 (ADR-CAT-015 also POL-CAT-011). Neither policy exists: ADR-CAT-031 decided that no POL-CAT-010 would be written.
findings.fix: Remove POL-CAT-010 and 011 from the traces of those ADRs.
